items.stem: In physical security risk analysis, risk is best understood as a function of:

options.rationale: Correct: risk combines the threat, the vulnerability to it, and the consequence if it is realised.
Threat by itself does not define risk without vulnerability and consequence.
Camera count is a control, not a definition of risk.
Budget is a constraint, not the definition of risk.

items.stem: A perimeter has excellent intrusion detection but almost no physical barriers. Why is this a design weakness?

options.text: Without delay, an intruder can reach the asset before responders arrive
options.rationale: Correct: detection must be paired with sufficient delay so response can interrupt before the asset is compromised.

options.text: Detection systems always cause false alarms
options.rationale: False alarms are a tuning issue, not the core weakness described here.
Barriers provide delay, a functional protection element.

options.text: Response time is irrelevant to design
options.rationale: Response time is central; delay must exceed response time to be effective.

items.explanation: Correct: detection must be paired with sufficient delay so response can interrupt before the asset is compromised.

items.stem: Select TWO activities that verify a physical protection system actually works as intended.

options.text: Performance testing of detection and delay elements
options.rationale: Correct: performance tests verify that detection and delay meet requirements.
Correct: commissioning against acceptance criteria confirms the system performs as specified.

options.text: Assuming vendor marketing claims are accurate
options.rationale: Marketing claims are not verification of real-world performance.
Skipping maintenance lets performance degrade, it does not verify it.

options.text: Counting the number of devices purchased
options.rationale: Device count does not demonstrate effectiveness.

items.explanation: Correct: performance tests verify that detection and delay meet requirements.
